title: Choosing and Using Backends
text: Variance components: bayesreml reports SDs lognormal priors; REML gives point estimates can zero (boundary). squaring bayesreml SDs, expect 5–15% differences small datasets. BLUPs vs posterior means: Rankings typically identical (r > 0.99). Bayesian estimates slightly shrunk due prior. Convergence: ASReml may fail complex models (AI singularity); bayesreml priors often succeeds REML fails. Computational cost: ASReml 10–100x faster. Use ASReml exploration, bayesreml final inference full uncertainty. bayesreml modifies data.table reference: Always use copy() passing data.table objects bayesreml.

text: Routine analysis: Use ASReml (fast, well-tested) Publication-quality inference: Run bayesreml credible intervals Model diagnostics: Compare – divergence signals weak identification prior sensitivity ASReml licence: bayesreml provides full functionality (slower)

title: Grain-Fill Case Study: FDA for Yield Prediction
text: crop variety trials, grain weight measured time grain-filling period. rate pattern grain fill may influence final yield. Traditional approaches fit parametric curves (logistic, Gompertz) plot extract parameters (rate, maximum). FDA provides flexible alternative: represent variety’s grain-fill trajectory smooth curve relate entire curve yield.

title: Grain-Fill Case Study: FDA for Yield Prediction
text: use simulated sim_grain_fill dataset: 20 varieties, 3 blocks, 8 time points (10–45 days anthesis).
code: library(funcrop) library(data.table)  data(sim_grain_fill) dt <- copy(sim_grain_fill) dt[, variety := factor(variety)] dt[, block := factor(block)] dt[, plot_id := factor(plot_id)]  # Add plot-level yield noise (original yield is per-variety) set.seed(42) pids <- unique(dt$plot_id) dt <- merge(dt,             data.table(plot_id = pids,                        yield_noise = rnorm(length(pids), 0, 0.8)),             by = "plot_id", sort = FALSE) dt[, yield_plot := yield + yield_noise]

title: Grain-Fill Case Study: FDA for Yield Prediction
code: times <- sort(unique(dt$time)) basis <- bspline_basis(times, n_knots = 4, degree = 3, penalty_order = 2) cat("Basis functions:", basis$n_basis, "\n") #> Basis functions: 8  # Evaluate at observation times B_obs <- bspline_basis(dt$time, n_knots = 4, degree = 3,                         boundary = basis$boundary)$B

title: Grain-Fill Case Study: FDA for Yield Prediction
text: Fit plot’s grain-fill trajectory OLS (mixed model yet):
code: plots <- unique(as.character(dt$plot_id)) alpha_hat <- matrix(NA, nrow = length(plots), ncol = ncol(B_obs)) rownames(alpha_hat) <- plots  for (p in seq_along(plots)) {   idx <- which(as.character(dt$plot_id) == plots[p])   y_p <- dt$grain_weight[idx]   B_p <- B_obs[idx, ]   alpha_hat[p, ] <- solve(crossprod(B_p), crossprod(B_p, y_p)) }  cat("Fitted", length(plots), "plot-level curves\n") #> Fitted 60 plot-level curves cat("Coefficient matrix:", nrow(alpha_hat), "x", ncol(alpha_hat), "\n") #> Coefficient matrix: 60 x 8

title: Grain-Fill Case Study: FDA for Yield Prediction
text: Average per-plot coefficients within variety: Variety-mean grain-fill curves (4 selected varieties).
code: pvm <- unique(data.table(plot_id = as.character(dt$plot_id),                           variety = as.character(dt$variety))) var_levels <- sort(unique(as.character(dt$variety))) n_var <- length(var_levels) n_basis <- ncol(B_obs)  alpha_variety <- matrix(NA, nrow = n_var, ncol = n_basis) rownames(alpha_variety) <- var_levels  for (v in var_levels) {   v_plots <- pvm[variety == v, plot_id]   alpha_variety[v, ] <- colMeans(alpha_hat[v_plots, , drop = FALSE]) }  # Reconstruct curves on a fine grid t_fine <- seq(min(times), max(times), length.out = 200) B_fine <- bspline_basis(t_fine, n_knots = 4, degree = 3,                          boundary = basis$boundary)$B curves <- B_fine %*% t(alpha_variety) show_vars <- var_levels[c(1, 5, 10, 15)] cols <- c("#440154", "#31688e", "#35b779", "#fde725")  plot(range(t_fine), range(curves[, show_vars]), type = "n",      xlab = "Days after anthesis", ylab = "Grain weight (g)",      main = "Variety-Mean Grain-Fill Curves") for (i in seq_along(show_vars)) {   lines(t_fine, curves[, show_vars[i]], col = cols[i], lwd = 2) } legend("topleft", legend = show_vars, col = cols, lwd = 2, bty = "n")

title: Grain-Fill Case Study: FDA for Yield Prediction
text: Compute functional covariate matrix regress yield :
code: # Inner product matrix J t_quad <- seq(min(times), max(times), length.out = 500) B_quad <- bspline_basis(t_quad, n_knots = 4, degree = 3,                          boundary = basis$boundary)$B J <- crossprod(B_quad) * diff(t_quad[1:2])  # Functional covariate: C = Alpha %*% J C_mat <- alpha_variety %*% as.matrix(J)  # Yield data yield_dt <- dt[, .(yield = mean(yield_plot)), keyby = variety]  # Simple OLS regression: yield ~ C reg_dt <- data.frame(   yield = yield_dt$yield[match(var_levels, yield_dt$variety)] ) for (k in seq_len(n_basis)) {   reg_dt[[paste0("C", k)]] <- C_mat[, k] }  fit_ols <- lm(as.formula(paste("yield ~",                paste0("C", 1:n_basis, collapse = " + "))),               data = reg_dt)  cat("R-squared:", round(summary(fit_ols)$r.squared, 3), "\n") #> R-squared: 0.655 cat("RMSE:", round(sqrt(mean(fit_ols$residuals^2)), 3), "\n") #> RMSE: 1.111

title: Grain-Fill Case Study: FDA for Yield Prediction
text: regression coefficients b define importance function beta(t) = sum_k b_k * B_k(t): Coefficient function beta(t): phase grain-fill influences yield. Interpretation: beta(t) large positive, grain-fill time contributes positively yield. beta(t) near zero, phase unimportant. identifies critical growth window breeders.
code: b_hat <- coef(fit_ols)[paste0("C", 1:n_basis)] beta_t <- as.numeric(B_fine %*% b_hat)  plot(t_fine, beta_t, type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "#440154",      xlab = "Days after anthesis", ylab = expression(beta(t)),      main = expression("Coefficient Function " * beta(t))) abline(h = 0, lty = 2, col = "grey50")

title: Construct a B-Spline Basis with Difference Penalty — bspline_basis
text: x Numeric vector evaluation points (e.g., time, wavelength, depth). Must contain least 2 unique values NA non-finite values. n_knots Integer; number internal knots. Default 10. Must least 1. total number basis functions n_knots + degree + 1. degree Integer; polynomial degree B-spline. Default 3 (cubic). Must >= 0. knot_type Character; method placing internal knots. One "equally_spaced" (default), "quantile", "custom". "custom", knots argument must supplied. knots Numeric vector internal knots. Required knot_type = "custom", ignored otherwise. Must lie strictly within boundary knots. boundary Numeric vector length 2 giving boundary knots (lower, upper). Defaults range(x) extended 1% side. penalty_order Integer; order difference penalty matrix. Default 2 (second-order differences, penalising curvature). Must least 1 less n_basis.

title: Construct a B-Spline Basis with Difference Penalty — bspline_basis
text: S3 object class "fda_basis" (list) containing: B Basis matrix (n x p), n = length(x) p = n_basis = n_knots + degree + 1. knots Numeric vector internal knots used. boundary Numeric vector length 2; boundary knots. degree Integer; polynomial degree. penalty_order Integer; order difference penalty. P Penalty matrix (p x p); sparse Matrix class dgCMatrix. Constructed D'D D difference matrix specified order. x Numeric vector; original evaluation points. n_basis Integer; total number basis functions. knot_type Character; knot placement method used.

title: Construct a B-Spline Basis with Difference Penalty — bspline_basis
text: basis matrix computed using splines::splineDesign(), handles boundary evaluation correctly. Knots augmented repeated boundary knots required B-spline recursion. penalty matrix \(P = D_d^T D_d\) encodes discrete approximation d-th derivative penalty, \(D_d\) d-th order difference matrix operating B-spline coefficients (Eilers & Marx, 1996).

text: Functional data analysis methods crop variety trials using B-spline basis functions integrated linear mixed models. Supports scalar--function regression relating primary traits (e.g., yield) secondary functional traits (e.g., grain-fill rate, stay-green) measured time. Handles two-dimensional functional traits (time x depth, time x wavelength) via tensor product B-splines, multi-environment trial (MET) analyses genotype--environment (GxE) interaction. Provides dual-backend architecture: ASReml-R (REML estimation) bayesreml (Bayesian MCMC via greta), pedigree genomic relationship matrix support. Includes publication-ready visualisation tools functional profiles, coefficient functions, GxE patterns.

what: Reparameterise B-Spline Basis for Mixed Model Representation — make_Zspline
title: Reparameterise B-Spline Basis for Mixed Model Representation — make_Zspline
text: Decomposes B-spline basis fixed-effect (X) random-effect (Z) components, enabling equivalence penalised splines linear mixed models (Wand, 2003; Wood, 2017). essential fitting P-splines via REML mixed model software (e.g., ASReml-R, lme4).

title: Reparameterise B-Spline Basis for Mixed Model Representation — make_Zspline
code: make_Zspline(basis, constraint = c("decompose", "absorb"))

title: Reparameterise B-Spline Basis for Mixed Model Representation — make_Zspline
text: basis object class "fda_basis" (returned bspline_basis()). constraint Character; reparameterisation method. One : "decompose" (Default) Spectral decomposition penalty matrix. Eigenvectors corresponding zero eigenvalues form fixed effects (X, null space), whilst positive eigenvalues form random effects (Z, range space), scaled inverse square root eigenvalues. "absorb" Absorb penalty Z via Cholesky decomposition Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse. resulting Z identity penalty structure, convenient standard mixed model software.

title: Reparameterise B-Spline Basis for Mixed Model Representation — make_Zspline
text: list components: X Fixed-effect design matrix (n x d), d = penalty_order dimension null space penalty. Typically contains polynomial terms degree penalty_order - 1. Z Random-effect design matrix (n x r), r = n_basis - d. "decompose" method, columns orthogonal; "absorb" method, penalty absorbed implied penalty random effect coefficients identity. penalty Sparse penalty matrix Z component. Identity matrix (dimension r x r) "absorb" method; identity "decompose" eigenvalues appropriately absorbed Z. rank Integer; rank original penalty matrix (n_basis - penalty_order). null_dim Integer; dimension null space (= penalty_order). constraint Character; method used.

title: Reparameterise B-Spline Basis for Mixed Model Representation — make_Zspline
text: key identity exploited : penalised spline fit minimising $$\|y - B\beta\|^2 + \lambda \beta^T P \beta$$ equivalent BLUP mixed model $$y = X\alpha + Z u + \varepsilon$$ \(u \sim N(0, \sigma_u^2 )\) smoothing parameter \(\lambda = \sigma^2 / \sigma_u^2\) estimated via REML. "decompose": spectral decomposition \(P = U \Lambda U^T\) separates null space (zero eigenvalues, giving X) range space (positive eigenvalues, giving Z scaled \(\Lambda^{-1/2}\)). "absorb": uses pseudoinverse \(P^+\) Cholesky factor \(L\) \(P^+ = LL^T\). \(Z = B_{\text{range}} L\) absorbs penalty, yielding identity covariance.

title: Reparameterise B-Spline Basis for Mixed Model Representation — make_Zspline
text: Wand, M.P. (2003). Smoothing mixed models. Computational Statistics, 18(2), 223–249. Wood, S.N. (2017). Generalized Additive Models: Introduction R (2nd ed.). Chapman & Hall/CRC.

title: Reparameterise B-Spline Basis for Mixed Model Representation — make_Zspline
code: x <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 100) basis <- bspline_basis(x, n_knots = 10, degree = 3)  # Decompose method (default) mm <- make_Zspline(basis, constraint = "decompose") dim(mm$X) #> [1] 100   2 dim(mm$Z) #> [1] 100  12  # Absorb method -- penalty becomes identity mm2 <- make_Zspline(basis, constraint = "absorb") dim(mm2$Z) #> [1] 100  12

what: Construct a Genomic Relationship Matrix — make_genomic_matrix
title: Construct a Genomic Relationship Matrix — make_genomic_matrix
text: Computes genomic relationship matrix (G) marker data using VanRaden (2008) Method 1 Method 2. convenience function; users may also supply pre-computed matrices fitting functions directly.

title: Construct a Genomic Relationship Matrix — make_genomic_matrix
code: make_genomic_matrix(   markers,   method = c("vanraden1", "vanraden2"),   min_maf = 0.01,   scale = TRUE )

title: Construct a Genomic Relationship Matrix — make_genomic_matrix
text: markers Numeric matrix dimension n_varieties x n_markers. Coded 0, 1, 2 (minor allele counts) -1, 0, 1 (centred). Row names identify varieties; column names (present) identify markers. method Character: "vanraden1" (default) "vanraden2". VanRaden Method 1: \(G = ZZ' / (2 \sum p_j(1-p_j))\), \(Z_{ij} = M_{ij} - 2p_j\) \(p_j\) allele frequency marker \(j\). VanRaden Method 2: \(G = ZDZ' / n_m\), \(D = \mathrm{diag}(1/(2 p_j (1-p_j)))\). min_maf Numeric: minimum minor allele frequency filter. Markers MAF threshold removed. Default 0.01. scale Logical: TRUE (default), scale G mean diagonal equals 1.

title: Construct a Genomic Relationship Matrix — make_genomic_matrix
text: symmetric positive (semi-)definite matrix dimension n_varieties x n_varieties, row/colnames rownames(markers).

text: Builds two-dimensional tensor product basis two marginal B-spline bases, suitable modelling functional data observed two indices (e.g., time x depth, time x wavelength). penalty standard additive Kronecker sum: \(P = P_1 \otimes I_2 + I_1 \otimes P_2\).

title: Construct a Tensor Product B-Spline Basis — tensor_bspline_basis
text: x1 Numeric vector evaluation points first dimension. x2 Numeric vector evaluation points second dimension. Must length x1 (.e., observation coordinates (x1[], x2[])). n_knots1, n_knots2 Integer; number internal knots marginal basis. Defaults 10. degree1, degree2 Integer; polynomial degree marginal basis. Defaults 3 (cubic). knot_type1, knot_type2 Character; knot placement marginal basis. One "equally_spaced" (default), "quantile", "custom". penalty_order1, penalty_order2 Integer; order difference penalty marginal basis. Defaults 2.

title: Construct a Tensor Product B-Spline Basis — tensor_bspline_basis
text: S3 object class c("fda_tensor_basis", "fda_basis") containing: B Tensor product basis matrix (n x p1p2), constructed row-wise Kronecker product two marginal basis matrices. basis1 marginal fda_basis object first dimension. basis2 marginal fda_basis object second dimension. P Combined additive penalty matrix (p1p2 x p1p2), sparse. Computed \(P_1 \otimes I_2 + I_1 \otimes P_2\). P1 Marginal penalty tensor product form: \(P_1 \otimes I_2\) (sparse). P2 Marginal penalty tensor product form: \(I_1 \otimes P_2\) (sparse). n_basis Integer; total number tensor product basis functions (p1 times p2).

title: Construct a Tensor Product B-Spline Basis — tensor_bspline_basis
text: tensor product basis matrix observation : $$B_{\text{tensor}}[,] = B_1[,] \otimes B_2[,]$$ \(\otimes\) denotes Kronecker product two row vectors. additive penalty: $$P = P_1 \otimes I_2 + I_1 \otimes P_2$$ penalises roughness dimension separately, standard approach tensor product P-splines (Marx & Eilers, 2005; Wood, 2006). Sparse matrix representations (Matrix package) used throughout tensor product bases can large (p1 * p2 basis functions).

title: Construct a Tensor Product B-Spline Basis — tensor_bspline_basis
text: Marx, B.D. Eilers, P.H.C. (2005). Multidimensional penalized signal regression. Technometrics, 47(1), 13–22. Wood, S.N. (2006). Low-rank scale-invariant tensor product smooths generalized additive mixed models. Biometrics, 62(4), 1025–1036.
